note: Investigation before any edit. Read all six cloudbuild*.yaml files. Five (conformant, f10-cad-loop, p2-juris, parcel-record-fill, publish) share the identical defect shape: a static _IMAGE_TAG default, built/pushed/described/listed under that fixed tag, with only a presence-only digest check (test -n "$$DIGEST") before the digest-pin deploy. cloudbuild.yaml (factory-snapshot) already uses $COMMIT_SHA and was excluded as out-of-scope (it does not race; its digest check is left unstrengthened, noted as a minor inconsistency in the close). No existing test file references cloudbuild.*.yaml's tag mechanism; runbook 90_runbooks/factory_cloud_job_execute.md does not mention _IMAGE_TAG or the tag convention at all (confirmed via grep, zero matches) -- nothing to update there.
designChosen: Suffix every ${_IMAGE}:${_IMAGE_TAG} reference with -$BUILD_ID (Cloud Build's own built-in substitution, guaranteed unique per submission, auto-populated with no caller change required for either triggered or manual gcloud builds submit invocations). Rejected alternative: baking $BUILD_ID into the _IMAGE_TAG substitution's own default value in the substitutions: block -- Cloud Build substitution defaults are literal strings, not re-scanned for built-in expansion, so this would not reliably expand; verified by checking Cloud Build's documented substitution resolution order rather than assuming. The chosen approach (suffix at each use site) is the mechanically simplest form that is certain to work, matching the dispatch's 'keep it simple and mechanical' instruction.
digestCheckStrengthened: test -n "$$DIGEST" (presence-shaped, one input) replaced with [[ "$$DIGEST" =~ ^${_IMAGE}@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] (shape-validated). Verified the real output format live before trusting the regex: gcloud artifacts docker images describe ... --format='value(image_summary.fully_qualified_digest)' against a real pushed image returned the full IMAGE_PATH@sha256:HASH form, confirming the regex's assumption rather than guessing it -- getting this wrong would have broken every future deploy job.
falsifierPreRegistered: Submit two overlapping gcloud builds submit runs of the SAME cloudbuild file (chosen: cloudbuild.p2-juris.yaml, the smallest single-job file, least likely to collide with the parallel session's active cards). If the fix works, each build's own describe step reads back exactly the digest it itself pushed, regardless of timing overlap -- verifiable directly from each build's own logs (Successfully tagged / digest: lines), not from a difference in the final digests (which could coincidentally match or differ regardless of the fix, since both builds have identical source).
